text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds fell into negative territory in late post-bourse trade on Thursday afternoon as a fall in U.S. Treasuries dragged German debt lower in thin pre-Easter trade. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.88, down 0.35 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended near their lows on Thursday, as U.S. Treasuries subsided ahead of the four-day Easter break. Earlier, the June gilt had pushed up as high as 109-13. It settled 8/32 lower on the day at 108-31. The gilt/Bund spread edged wider to 188 basis points from 185 late on Wednesday. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-27/32, down 12/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French 10-year bond futures settle higher but off peaks as investors cut positions ahead of four-day Easter holiday weekend. 3-month Pibor lifted by non-resident buying. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.28 up 0.08 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets ending close to day's lows with volumes thin ahead of four-day Easter weekend in most European markets. LIFFE closed Friday but Italy open, although closed Monday. Btps slid along with other markets. Market tried to go up on cabinet approval of mini-budget but failed to sustain move. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.88 down 0.50 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries turn sharply lower as 7.0 barrier breaks. Rumors have a large bank selling in a thin market. Some see delayed reaction to Thursday's negative data Worry increases on next week's NAPM, payrolls reports Volume expected to taper off as early close nears. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-21/32, down 26/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.06 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) recover some lost ground after Tokyo market hit by view Japanese financial system worries would ease following report Nippon Credit may withdraw from overseas ops. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.62, down 0.22 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market supply ceased on Thursday ahead of the four-day Easter holiday. The market will be closed for Good Friday and Easter Monday and will resume trade on Tuesday. In the late session the Swedish Export Credit set a 125 million stg Oct 1999 bond via Daiwa. It pays a 6.25 pct coupon. In the emerging market sector next week, Ecuador will embark on a series of investor presentations for its debut Eurobond.
